### Observed differences

- In the later window, A01 runs much later in each case: its median relative position moved from about one-sixth of the trace to about two-thirds (mean 0.26 to 0.65), while it still appears in every trace in both windows. [POS001]
- The order between A01 and the other main activities flipped. Before, A01 came first in mixed proportions (before A02 in about 55 in 100 traces, A04 in about 49, A05 in about 80, A07 in about 68); in the later window A04 and A07 always precede A01, A02 precedes it in about 81 in 100, and A05 in about 63 in 100. Both activities of each pair co-occur in every trace throughout. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]
- Direct succession moved in step. In the later window, A07 leads directly to A01 in about 68 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions (before about 18 in 100), and A04 leads mostly to A07 (about 70 in 100, before 54 in 100) while its direct transition to A01 is no longer observed (before about 16 in 100). A01's outgoing traffic now goes to A03 in about 47 in 100 (before about 7 in 100), and A04 and A07 no longer appear among A01's observed successors (before about 18 and 7 in 100). [DIR001, DIR003, DIR004]
- Pair distances agree: A07→A01 is direct in about 68 in 100 of traces (before 54 in 100 of only 65 traces; now all 200), A04→A01 is typically two steps apart with no direct transitions left, A01→A03 is direct in about 47 in 100 traces, and A02→A01 and A05→A01 gaps lengthened (direct A02→A01 fell from about 57 in 100 to about 13 in 100; direct A05→A01 from about 36 in 100 to about 11 in 100, on 39 and 126 traces). [LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG007]
- A02, A05 and A07 each shifted slightly earlier (mean relative position down by about 0.08–0.10 of the trace). [POS002, POS003, POS004]
- Smaller shifts: A02's outgoing traffic moved from A01 (about 26 in 100) to A05 (about 40 in 100); A07's direct transition to A03 is no longer observed (about 28 in 100 before); A01→A05 within five steps appears in fewer traces (74 of 200 vs 161 of 200), though it is direct when it occurs (about 72 in 100 vs 38 in 100). [DIR002, LAG002, LAG008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The number of qualifying items (21, all control-flow) is far above the roughly 0.18 expected for an unchanged process, so sampling variation cannot account for the pattern as a whole. The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01's placement changed: it moved from an early position to a late position in the case. Before, A01 ran near the start, typically before A02, A04, A05 and A07, with no fixed order against A02 and A04; in the later window A04 and A07 always precede it (A04 chaining through A07 into A01), A02 usually precedes it, A05 precedes it in about 63 in 100 traces (that relation stays mixed), and A01 now closes the flow, leading directly to A03 in about half the traces. [POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, LAG001, LAG004, LAG007]

The hypothesis rests on direct positional and relational evidence: A01's position distribution shifted by about 0.39 of the trace with full support in both windows, the A01–A04 and A01–A07 relations changed from mixed to fixed order (a changed ordering constraint, not a path-frequency shift), and the successor and distance changes point the same way. Participation itself did not change — every activity involved appears in all traces in both windows. Limitations: positions are event positions, not clock times, so only order within the case is established; and the evidence cannot distinguish A01 itself moving to the end from the block of A02/A04/A05/A07 being regrouped before it, since only relative order is observed. [POS001, REL002, REL004, DIR004, LAG007]

Other differences: the slight advance of A02, A05 and A07, A02's rerouting from A01 toward A05, the loss of A07's direct transition to A03, and the rarer A01→A05 co-occurrence within five steps are consistent side-effects of the same reordering but are not needed to support it. [DIR002, LAG002, LAG008, POS002, POS003, POS004]
